Regarding Shelta, a secret language used by Irish Travelers, it has loanwords that have been borrowed by mainstream English speakers, such as the word "bloke" meaning 'a man' in the mid-19th century. There is no standard orthography for Shelta. Broadly speaking, it can either be written following an Irish-type orthography or an English-type orthography. For example, the word for 'married' can either be spelled lósped or lohsped; the word for 'woman' can either be spelled mná or mena.
